# SOP-P1-L4-04 Shift handover - Heat Treat line

Revision: Rev E  
Plant: P1, line P1-L4  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, EQ-P1-L4-HT03

Purpose
1. Define the standardized shift handover procedure for the Heat Treat line to ensure continuity of operations, safe transfer of process state, and traceable records. This SOP applies to operators and technicians assigned to P1-L4 and interfacing maintenance staff.

Preconditions
2. The departing operator must have completed the shift checklist and all required log entries. All critical alarms must be acknowledged and cleared. Any open maintenance requests must be recorded per MM-P1-L4-CN01. If material or product disposition is unresolved, the issue shall be escalated to the shift supervisor before handover.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
3. Required PPE for handover activities on the Heat Treat line: safety glasses, heat-resistant gloves, and hearing protection. Use of additional PPE for charged work or maintenance follows MM-P1-L4-CN01 and facility rules.

Background and rationale
4. The Heat Treat line comprises the CNC turning center, hydraulic press, and heat treat furnace identified as EQ-P1-L4-CN01, EQ-P1-L4-HP02, and EQ-P1-L4-HT03 respectively. Accurate transfer of machine state, process setpoints, and outstanding actions reduces scrap, prevents unplanned downtime, and maintains compliance with quality controls cited in QS-PROC-05. The austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C; this setpoint must be verified during each handover to confirm process readiness and to flag any deviation requiring QA notification per QS-PROC-05.

Step-by-step handover procedure
5. Handover start
   5.1 The incoming operator shall arrive at the workstation before the recorded end time of the outgoing shift to allow a full verbal and visual transfer.  
   5.2 Confirm identity of both parties and sign the on-shift log to indicate participation in the handover.

6. Visual and physical tour
   6.1 Perform a walk-through of the line with the departing operator. Check EO status lights, guard integrity, and tool storage.  
   6.2 Confirm material staging and label status. Note any deviations or nonconforming parts in the shift log.

7. Machine state verification
   7.1 EQ-P1-L4-CN01: Verify program loaded and tool offsets saved. Confirm that spindle warm-up has been completed; the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) is 15 minutes and must be completed prior to production restart. Record the warm-up completion time in the machine log.  
   7.2 EQ-P1-L4-HP02: Confirm press is at rest, safeguards engaged, and that hydraulic parameters are at nominal operating state per MM-P1-L4-CN01. Note any leaks or abnormal noises observed during tour.  
   7.3 EQ-P1-L4-HT03: Verify furnace status and confirm the austenitizing setpoint for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #3 (EQ-P1-L4-HT03) is 880 °C. Confirm ramp programs and soak timers are as documented in the job packet. Any discrepancy with the 880 °C value requires immediate notification to quality per QS-PROC-05.

8. Alarms and events review
   8.1 Review the alarm history and event log for each piece of equipment. For any unresolved alarms, document the alarm code and corrective actions taken to date. Reference MM-P1-L4-CN01 for troubleshooting guidance and SB-1046 for legacy advisory notes where applicable.

9. Material and work order status
   9.1 Confirm active work orders and lot numbers. Verify inventory on the line matches the work order requirements. Record any shortfalls and expected replenishment actions.  
   9.2 Confirm that all processed parts are labeled and segregated per QS-PROC-05 if they are nonconforming.

10. Quality and inspection
   10.1 Review recent inspection records and sample results. If any trending issues or out-of-spec data exist, document the issue and required hold or rework action. Communicate open quality items to the incoming operator and shift supervisor.

11. Maintenance and safety issues
   11.1 Document any maintenance tasks in the maintenance system and verify that urgent items are flagged in MM-P1-L4-CN01.  
   11.2 Confirm that lockout/tagout status of any isolated equipment is visible and that tags are current. If tags are present, the responsible technician must be identified in the handover log.

12. Records to keep
   12.1 Maintain the shift handover form in the line binder and enter a summary in the electronic log. Include: machine state, confirmation of austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 as 880 °C, confirmation that spindle warm-up for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 completed with the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) recorded as 15 minutes, open issues, and any quality holds.  
   12.2 Retain copies of the signed handover sheet and attach relevant printouts from equipment event logs. Reference QS-PROC-05 for retention guidelines.

Examples and common scenarios
13. Example A — Incoming operator finds furnace setpoint different from 880 °C: Escalate to quality per QS-PROC-05, place the current batch on hold, document the deviation on the handover form, and notify maintenance via MM-P1-L4-CN01 if required.  
14. Example B — Spindle warm-up was not completed: Do not start production cycles. Complete the spindle warm-up process and log the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) as 15 minutes before resuming machining.

Handover sign-off
15. Signatures: The departing operator, incoming operator, and shift supervisor must sign the handover sheet. Required entries: names, start and end of coverage confirmation, verification of austenitizing setpoint for EQ-P1-L4-HT03 as 880 °C, and confirmation that spindle warm-up for EQ-P1-L4-CN01 was completed with the spindle warm-up time for Heat Treat CNC turning center #1 (EQ-P1-L4-CN01) recorded as 15 minutes. Attach any supporting logs or printouts.

Related documents
16. See MM-P1-L4-CN01 for maintenance procedures, QS-PROC-05 for quality handling and disposition, and SB-1046 for service bulletin references.

Deviation and escalation
17. Any procedural deviation during handover that impacts safety, product quality, or machine integrity must be escalated immediately to the shift supervisor and documented in the handover records. Use the related documents listed above for further action.
